title: Metals and Non-metals
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Metals and Non-metals Worksheets (Reactivity Series, Acids, Oxides)
standard_text: The order of metals and carbon in the reactivity series; the use of carbon in obtaining metals from metal oxides; properties of ceramics, polymers and composites (qualitative); the chemical properties of metal and non-metal oxides with respect to acidity; reactions of acids with metals to produce a salt plus hydrogen; displacement reactions.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on metals and non-metals: properties, metals with acids and oxygen, naming salts, acidic and basic oxides, the reactivity series and displacement. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one.
body_html:
How to think about it

Metals and non-metals have different properties and reactions.

  • Metals are shiny, conduct heat and electricity, and are malleable. Non-metals are usually dull, brittle and poor conductors.
  • metal + acid → salt + hydrogen; metal + oxygen → metal oxide. Metal oxides are basic; non-metal oxides are acidic.
  • A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compounds.
Example

Zinc + sulfuric acid → ?

Sulfuric → sulfate

Answer: zinc sulfate + hydrogen

Example

Copper in magnesium sulfate: reaction?

Copper is less reactive

Answer: no reaction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all metals are magnetic.
  • Thinking the gas from metal + acid is oxygen.
  • Thinking a less reactive metal can displace a more reactive one.

faq.q: What is made when a metal reacts with an acid?
faq.a: A salt and hydrogen gas. For example, magnesium + hydrochloric acid → magnesium chloride + hydrogen.

faq.q: How do you name the salt?
faq.a: The metal's name comes first. Hydrochloric acid makes chlorides, sulfuric acid makes sulfates and nitric acid makes nitrates.
A more reactive metal takes the place of a less reactive metal in a compound, for example iron + copper sulfate → iron sulfate + copper.

potassium, sodium, calcium, magnesium, aluminium, zinc, iron, copper, silver, gold
